Project 6: statci — Statistical CI/CD, Calibration Fuzzing & Manuscript Auditor

Suggested GitHub Repo: statci
GitHub One-Liner: Automated statistical CI/CD for R: static bug linting, Simulation-Based Calibration fuzzing, manuscript-to-code auditing, and adversarial robustness suites.
Topics: r-package, ci-cd, statistical-verification, simulation-based-calibration, quarto, static-analysis, open-science, reproducibility

Project Statement

Software engineers rely on continuous integration, static analyzers, and fuzz tests to catch silent bugs before shipping code—yet statistical analyses and quantitative methods packages often reach peer review with undetected flaws: unseeded stochastic steps, parallel RNG seed collisions, silent factor-level drops, uncentered Level-1 predictors causing contextual confounding, biased custom estimators, or copy-pasted numbers in manuscripts that no longer match the underlying model objects. As AI accelerates code generation and models grow more computationally complex, manual spot-checking is no longer enough.

statci brings automated CI/CD and adversarial verification to statistical R code and Quarto/RMarkdown manuscripts. It combines an AST-based statistical linter that catches silent methodological traps, an automated calibration and fuzzing harness (Simulation-Based Calibration, Type-I error checks, parallel RNG invariance tests, non-convergence auditing), a manuscript-to-code consistency auditor that verifies reported numbers against saved R model objects, and an adversarial sensitivity battery—all packaged with ready-to-use GitHub Actions templates and clean pass/warn/fail HTML audit reports.

Why Existing R Tools Aren’t Enough

  • lintr checks code style (spacing, line length), not statistical or methodological correctness (centering traps, parallel RNG safety, data leakage, unseeded stochasticity).
  • statcheck only checks internal p-value arithmetic in APA strings via regex—it cannot inspect your R code, verify whether numbers match actual fitted model objects, or stress-test your estimator via simulation.
  • testthat tests deterministic code logic, not probabilistic statistical properties like Type-I error calibration, coverage, or estimator stability under data perturbations.

Core Architectural Pillars

  1. AST-Based Statistical Linter: Parses R scripts and Quarto/Rmd code chunks to flag methodological hazards—unseeded stochastic calls, unsafe parallel RNG (mclapply/foreach without L’Ecuyer streams), missing-data silent listwise mismatches, uncentered predictors in multilevel interaction terms, and preprocessing-before-split data leakage.
  2. Estimator Calibration & Fuzzing Harness: Given any user-supplied data-generating function and estimator, automatically runs parameter-recovery checks, Simulation-Based Calibration (SBC) / Type-I error calibration tests, multi-core RNG invariance checks, and non-convergence/singular-fit audits.
  3. Manuscript-to-Code Consistency Auditor: Parses Quarto/Rmd manuscripts alongside saved R model artifacts to cross-check inline estimates, standard errors, p-values, CIs, and sample sizes—catching stale copy-paste discrepancies automatically.
  4. Adversarial Sensitivity & Robustness Battery: Automatically re-runs fitted pipelines under structured stress tests (outlier winsorizing, cluster leave-one-out, alternative missingness handling, bootstrap perturbations), optionally inside an isolated container, and produces a unified pass/warn/fail audit report plus a GitHub Actions workflow template.

v1 Definition of Done

  • Extensible AST rule engine shipping 10+ well-tested statistical lint rules for R scripts and Quarto documents.
  • Working estimator verification suite (Type-I error, coverage/bias recovery, parallel RNG invariance, convergence auditing) with clear statistical pass/fail thresholds accounting for Monte Carlo error.
  • Working Quarto-to-R-object numerical cross-checker and adversarial sensitivity runner.
  • HTML/Markdown audit report generator, GitHub Actions CI generator (use_statci_github_action()), exhaustive testthat suite, vignettes, and clean R CMD check.

New-Conversation Handoff Block

We are starting a new flagship, CRAN-grade R package in this repository: `statci` — an automated statistical CI/CD, calibration fuzzing, manuscript-to-code auditing, and adversarial robustness suite for R.

Project mission: Bring software-engineering-grade continuous verification to statistical R pipelines, methods packages, and Quarto manuscripts:
1. AST-based statistical linter for R scripts and Quarto/Rmd chunks detecting real methodological hazards (unseeded randomness, unsafe parallel RNG, uncentered predictors in multilevel interactions, data leakage, silent factor/missingness drops).
2. Automated estimator verification & fuzzing harness: given a DGP + fitting function, run Type-I error calibration, coverage/bias recovery, parallel RNG invariance across core counts, and non-convergence/singular-fit auditing (accounting for Monte Carlo SE).
3. Manuscript-to-code consistency auditor cross-checking inline numbers, sample sizes, CIs, and p-values in Quarto/Rmd manuscripts against actual R model objects.
4. Adversarial sensitivity battery (outlier perturbations, cluster leave-one-out, missingness/bootstrap checks) outputting a clean pass/warn/fail HTML/Markdown audit report + a GitHub Actions workflow template (`use_statci_github_action()`).

Please start by inspecting this repo, designing the rule engine and verification architecture (`ARCHITECTURE.md`) and phased build plan, and then we will build iteratively to full `testthat` coverage, vignettes, and a clean `R CMD check`.
